ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Ida B. Wells

code.originalText: Two weeks after starting losartan: potassium, creatinine and blood pressure, and the decision about dapagliflozin

text.paragraph: Two weeks after starting losartan: potassium, creatinine and blood pressure, and the decision about dapagliflozin. [S]

Mrs. Wells returns two weeks after starting losartan 50 mg, atorvastatin and vitamin D3. She has had no dizziness, cough or swelling of the lips. Her home readings average 140/84. Her ankles swell less. She met the dietitian this morning and is cutting salt, and she has read about SGLT2 inhibitors and asked how much they lower the risk of kidney failure; the trial evidence in people with and without diabetes was explained. She wants to start. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-02-03; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 142/84, pulse 74; weight 69.6 kg
Regular rhythm; no ankle swelling today

Tiredness for some months and ankle swelling by evening, with a raised creatinine (1.42 mg/dL, race-free eGFR 40, confirmed at 38 with cystatin C) and albumin in the urine (240 mg/g) found today; cause and chronicity to be established
S — Synthetic presenting finding, superseded by the kidney diagnosis at two weeks.
Elevated blood pressure at intake (164/94 mmHg, average of two readings), without a diagnosis of hypertension; home readings for one week to confirm
S — Synthetic presenting finding, superseded by the confirmed diagnosis at two weeks.
Hypertension, stage 2, confirmed by home readings (average 150/88 mmHg), with chronic kidney disease
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; no blood pressure from her life is recorded.

Chronic kidney disease G3b A2 (eGFR 38 by creatinine and cystatin C, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 240 and 228 mg/g), present at least two years; small, echogenic kidneys without obstruction; most likely hypertensive kidney disease, with APOL1-associated disease possible; 5-year kidney failure risk about 7%
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to the kidney disease recorded at her death.
Anemia of chronic kidney disease, mild (hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL) with adequate iron stores; a likely part of her tiredness
Vitamin D deficiency (25-hydroxyvitamin D 17 ng/mL) with a mildly raised PTH (84 pg/mL); calcium and phosphate normal
S — Synthetic laboratory finding, part of the mineral and bone check in kidney disease.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024); KDIGO 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Blood Pressure in Chronic Kidney Disease (2021); Executive summary of the 2017 KDIGO Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral and Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD) Guideline Update (2017); 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, anemia and depression monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Annual wellness visit in two weeks. Potassium and creatinine in four weeks. Call for dizziness, fainting, vomiting or diarrhea (hold dapagliflozin and losartan that day), or genital itching. Next scheduled visit 2026-02-17: subsequent annual wellness visit. [S]
